title: CIAM for AI: Authn/Authz for Agents — Michael Grinich, CEO of WorkOS
talk_summary: A WorkOS CEO argues agents need first-class identity (headless login, scoped delegation, audit trails) and surveys four patterns: persona shadowing, delegation chains, capability tokens, and human escalation.

takeaways.technique: Middleware trust boundary between agents and systems
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of baking permissions into agent code, put a managed layer between agentic code and the resources it touches that can log, enforce, and dynamically scope actions, treating the agent as untrusted.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You kind of have to treat your agent as like untrusted. And so this idea of like putting a layer in between that's managed, that can be dynamic, that can actually log and enforce things

takeaways.technique: Persona shadowing (scoped agent identity per human/role)
takeaways.what_they_do: Give each agent a shadow identity derived from a real user/role with a strict subset of privileges, so every action is attributable and limits are enforceable at the identity layer.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you give an agent an identity that shadows a user... It has a subset of the privileges that a user might have

takeaways.technique: Capability tokens scoped to one action with expiry
takeaways.what_they_do: Mint short-lived, self-contained tokens granting exactly one capability (e.g. read X for 60 min) rather than long-lived broad API keys.
takeaways.evidence_quote: agent X can read Bob's calendar for the next 60 minutes you create a token just for that action... those can expire after a certain amount of time

takeaways.what_they_do: Pass signed tokens step-by-step through sub-agents so each link carries forward the original user's authorization and can be verified statelessly.
takeaways.evidence_quote: each link in the chain must carry forward the original user's authorization

takeaways.what_they_do: Bubble risky actions to a human for approve/deny, but the speaker warns users rubber-stamp everything, so it must be paired with scoping.
